comments.body:
That is interesting. I tested that when I was reviewing the lasted PR (collapse to single module), and again now with both fcrepo-webapp and fcrepo-webapp-plus in tomcat... and I am not seeing that behavior.
Without any port properties set, running Fedora in tomcat while building the master branch of fcrepo-import-export, the build completes successfully.

Have you verified this, Michael Durbin?

Bethany Seeger reported this on IRC, and since I knew I was remiss in testing it, I quickly wrote up the ticket. That said, in testing right now with another instance of apache-tomcat-7.0.69, I get the following error:

[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.codehaus.cargo:cargo-maven2-plugin:1.4.12:start (start-cargo) on project fcrepo-import-export: Execution start-cargo of goal org.codehaus.cargo:cargo-maven2-plugin:1.4.12:start failed: Port number 8009 (defined with the property cargo.tomcat.ajp.port) is in use. Please free it on the system or set it to a different port in the container configuration. -> [Help 1]

It's a relatively easy fix, but I'm going to spend my scant free time working the other issues with import first.
That would explain it. I am not using an AJP connector, hence port 8009 is disabled locally.

Bethany Seeger, would you be interested in taking this ticket? The solution is likely a combination of adding a new dynamic port for the integration tests:

  • https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/pom.xml#L99
  • https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/pom.xml#L123
  • https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/pom.xml#L253
Sure - I can take this on, but probably won't look at it till tomorrow or early next week. (not that I'm assuming there's a huge rush on this, but just in case that matters)
